questions.q: According to this lesson, which phrase best describes the capstone project in portfolio/interview terms?
options: "A stateful, multi-turn conversational application against a production LLM API"
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly contrasts the undersold 'I built a chatbot' with precise, demonstrable language like 'stateful, multi-turn conversational application against a production LLM API.'

questions.q: Which chapter does the lesson credit for the decision to use a system prompt instead of fine-tuning in the capstone?
questions.explain: Chapter 4 established that prompting should come before fine-tuning for most use cases — the capstone's system prompt is that principle applied directly.

questions.q: Of the four listed project extensions, which one draws on Lesson 17 specifically?
options: Adding error handling for dropped connections
Switching to a different programming language
Adding tool/function calling so the assistant can run a real function
questions.explain: Tool/function calling, covered in Lesson 17, lets the assistant call a real function (like a calculator) as a natural next extension of the capstone.

questions.q: Where does this course sit within the AI Engineer career path, per this lesson?
options: It is course 5 of 12 in the Job-Ready stage, with more courses still ahead
It is the very first course in the path
It is the final course in the path, with nothing left afterward
It is not part of any structured career path
questions.explain: Generative AI & LLMs is course 5 of 12 in the AI Engineer path's Job-Ready stage — it's a major milestone, not the end of the path.

questions.q: What is the name of the next course in the AI Engineer path after Generative AI & LLMs?
questions.explain: Per the AI Engineer path's course sequence, Prompt & Context Engineering comes directly after Generative AI & LLMs, building on the system prompts and message-shaping used casually in this capstone.
